subject: EdgeNova post-call: SLO boundaries, fallback architecture options
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Tim Jones <tim.jones@edgenova.com>, Alice Park <alice@edgenova.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T15:12:00Z
Subject: Recap: EdgeNova post-call — latency targets & topology options

Hi Tim / Alice,

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our call and the items we agreed to validate: we captured your primary pain points and initial SLO targets, plus three deployment approaches to evaluate. Please review and correct anything I missed.

Highlights from call:
- Pain: interactive product search and summarization currently nets p95 end-to-end latency ~600ms under peak; search UX suffers at >300ms.
- Goal: reduce p95 inference latency to <=120ms for short requests (<=512 tokens) and keep p99 under 300ms; sustained throughput target ~40 QPS across US region.
- Model: multilingual NLU + summarization; prefer 7B class model for quality but open to 1.6B for degraded fallback. Estimate avg request size ~350 tokens; peak bursts up to 800 tokens.
- Compliance: data residency ok in US; audit logs and SOC-2 evidence will be required for procurement.

Deployment options we sketched:
1) Hosted Dedicated pool (single-region A): predictable latency, Redwood-managed GPUs, automated autoscaling.
2) Private VPC (customer network): more isolation and direct peering, slightly higher setup lead time.
3) Hybrid multi-variant routing: primary 7B in Dedicated, fallback to 1.6B quantized variant in low-capacity situations or for non-critical traffic classes.

Suggested technical checkpoints (what Redwood will validate next):
- Synthetic microbenchmarks for your 7B model variant at 512/800 token lengths (we'll run both QPS and tail latency).
- KV/prefix caching profile: what fraction of requests are repeated or share common prefixes (this affects effective throughput).
- Traffic shape: 95/99 percentile request sizes and burst patterns over 1-minute windows.

Attachments: edgenova_inference_estimate.xlsx (cost sketch), slo-matrix.pdf (initial SLO table).

Next asks / proposed next steps:
1) If you can share a small anonymized sample of production requests or a synthetic profile, we can run an evaluation within our sandbox.
2) Schedule a 60-minute architecture workshop next week to map routing, KV cache placement, and autoscaling thresholds.
3) We'll prepare a detailed mutual action plan + procurement checklist upon confirmation.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Mina — thanks for the thorough recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- Our current infra tight point is cold-starts during batch deploys; if dedicated nodes are scaled up quickly we still see spikes. How much of that is mitigated by warm pools/KV caching?
- For the fallback 1.6B option: what quality delta should we expect on summarization? We need to understand acceptable degradation for specific business flows (billing vs. search).
- SOC-2 evidence: our procurement team will ask for the usual artifacts; please include your standard SOC-2 scope and retention policy.

I'll pull a week of anonymized request logs and drop them into a shared folder by Friday. Also, can you attach the sandbox access steps so our infra team can coordinate networking?

—Tim

Subject: Re: Recap: EdgeNova post-call — latency targets & topology options

Tim — quick technical notes from my side based on the targets you described:

Short answers up front:
- Warm pools + small pre-warmed KV cache will eliminate most cold-start tail spikes for short requests.
- For 7B class models on A100 80GB we estimate (continuous serving): p95 ~ 90-130ms at 40 QPS with 512 token avg when using optimized kernels + batching window ~15ms. p99 depends on burst smoothing and cache hit rates.
- Fallback to a 1.6B int8/quant variant is viable: expect a summarization quality drop of ~6-12% on our internal ROUGE/QA evals for long-form summarization; for short extraction tasks the delta is much smaller.

Proposed architectural baseline:
- Primary: redwood-7b-v2-q4 on Dedicated A100 pool in us-west1 with continuous batching.
- Secondary (degraded): redwood-1.6b-int8 in the same region but lower-cost instance class; route non-critical traffic here when latency SLO cannot be met.
- Caching: prefix KV store sized for top 10% prefixes (we'll recommend initial cache size after we see sample traffic).
- Autoscaling: target CPU/GPU utilization 60-70% steady-state; use burst buffer (hot spare nodes) to smooth minute-level spikes.
- Observability: per-route p50/p95/p99 token latency and tail token cost reporting wired into Redwood Console and your monitoring (we can export traces to your Datadog).

I attached a small table in the slack thread with expected token throughput per A100 instance and a rough cost arc — I'll convert to a formal estimate once we get sample traffic.

Connor
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
